topic: Blood transfusion and cross-matching in arthroplasty
usual_baseline: Too much blood is cross-matched and too much transfused. C:T ratios run from 3.21 in hip replacement to 16.6:1 in spine surgery. MSBOS compliance was 52% in one spinal unit. Of transfused hip patients, 24–46% were inappropriate. Transfusions often go unrecorded (26%) and blood loss is recorded in only 57%.
fix_that_works: Stopping routine cross-match for THR with a day 2 blood count: unused units fell 96%, C:T 3.21 to 1.62 [1426]. A revised spinal guideline aligned with MSBOS: compliance 52% to 72%, over-cross-matching 43% to 12% [1744]. An agreed cross-match tariff cut units from 664 to 58, though C:T only moved from 16.6 to 11.5 [1428].
fix_that_fails: Staff education and policy amendments after 27% of THR patients were transfused (46% inappropriate): no reduction in transfusion rates [1470]. Several audits proposed ordering schedules but never re-audited [1407] [1486].
consultant_advice: Cross-matching audits are done often and the fix is known: group and save, not cross-match. The harder question is who gets transfused and why. Audit transfusion triggers, single-unit transfusion and pre-operative anaemia; 57% of patients with Hb below 12 g/dl were transfused [1446].
